findings.detail: The durable codebase fix (Part B) — a new `mcp_reconcile_orphans` function invoked from `mcp_retire_sweep` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, committed as 627faccae8df — is not present in the repository working tree. Searches for `mcp_reconcile_orphans`, `mcp_retire_sweep`, `e4f3-1661-2319-4a76`, `627faccae8df`, and the new test functions all returned no matches. The change was pushed to Gerrit as change 2454 but has not been merged to the working tree. The ticket itself remains `in_progress` and explicitly states it will not be closed until change 2454 is Verified +1. The root defect (orphaned compose-mcp:<sha> images accumulating without reconciliation) is therefore not fixed in the codebase. The Part A one-time surgical reclaim is an operational action attested in the ticket with specifics (14 named images removed, disk usage 76%→62%, alarm ALARM→OK), but it is not a durable fix — the underlying leak mechanism remains unaddressed in code.
findings.remediation: Merge Gerrit change 2454 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2454) to main so that `mcp_reconcile_orphans` and its tests are present in the working tree, then record the Verified +1 vote and merge confirmation as a ticket comment with the commit SHA and timestamp.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
